research_questions.question: How should a disputed Texas governmental invoice and downstream subcontractor payment be controlled?
research_questions.scope: Texas governmental-entity vendor/subcontractor payment chain under Chapter 2251; dispute notice and statutory timing only.
research_questions.answer: Under §2251.042(a), the governmental entity must notify the vendor of an invoice error or disputed amount no later than the 21st day after invoice receipt and give a detailed statement of the disputed amount. If resolved for the vendor, interest on the unpaid balance starts from the §2251.021 overdue date; if resolved for the entity, the vendor submits a corrected invoice subject to that section. Separately, a vendor receiving the governmental payment must pay the subcontractor's appropriate share by the 10th day after receipt under §2251.022(a), with day 11 overdue. findings.claim: Under Publication 94-116, a lump-sum contractor generally pays tax on taxable supplies and does not charge the customer; a separated contract treats the contractor as retailer of incorporated materials and collects tax on those materials, while construction labor is not taxable.
findings.qualification: Texas sales/use tax, selected public works/payroll, and construction payment facts for Texas contractors and service businesses.

findings.claim: Texas SECO states DBRA applies to federally funded public-building/public-works contracts over $2,000; applicable DOL wage determinations and weekly certified payroll tracking are required in the described program.

findings.claim: Section 2251.021(a) uses the later of goods receipt, completed service or invoice receipt. For example, if goods arrive March 1, service completes March 10 and the invoice is received March 20, March 20 is the trigger; the ordinary payment becomes overdue on the 31st day after that date (the state payment guide describes payment as due by day 30). A qualifying political subdivision whose governing body meets once a month or less uses the 46th day under §2251.021(b). The legal-services state-agency exception in §2251.021(b-1) is a separate 46-day rule.
findings.qualification: Contract for goods or services with a Texas state agency or political subdivision; excludes legal advice on remedies and separate public-work bond claims.

findings.claim: The Comptroller describes the total nonresidential repair/remodeling charge as taxable, with separately stated building-permit fees paid on the customer's behalf excluded. New construction follows a different labor/material rule. Mixed new/remodel contracts and exemptions require the specified facts; neither an industry code nor an invoice label determines the answer.
findings.qualification: Texas sales/use tax, selected public works/payroll, and construction payment facts for Texas contractors and service businesses.

findings.claim: Under §2251.042(a), the governmental entity must notify the vendor of an invoice error or disputed amount no later than the 21st day after invoice receipt and give a detailed statement of the disputed amount. If resolved for the vendor, interest on the unpaid balance starts from the §2251.021 overdue date; if resolved for the entity, the vendor submits a corrected invoice subject to that section. Separately, a vendor receiving the governmental payment must pay the subcontractor's appropriate share by the 10th day after receipt under §2251.022(a), with day 11 overdue. The ledger should therefore preserve governmental receipt, dispute notice, resolution, corrected invoice and downstream receipt dates separately.
findings.qualification: Texas governmental-entity vendor/subcontractor payment chain under Chapter 2251; dispute notice and statutory timing only.

research_questions.question: What changed in the observed customer-support deployment, and whose results differed?
research_questions.scope: Two original empirical studies reviewed from public NBER/arXiv and HBS/Organization Science materials; evidence concerns workplace AI assistance, not accounting-agent performance.
research_questions.answer: In a staggered workplace deployment, an AI chat assistant improved customer-support resolution productivity but effects varied sharply by worker skill, and the study did not measure accounting or aggregate employment outcomes.

source_locators.locator: Public author/arXiv version, sections 2.2-2.3, 3.1-3.2, 4 and 5; lines 99-128, 227-251, 254-260 in accessed rendering.

observed_outcomes: 3 million chats associated with 5,179 agents; 1.2 million post-AI chats associated with 1,636 agents
13.8% increase in successfully resolved chats per hour in the author version; published QJE abstract reports 15% for 5,172 agents, so edition-specific figures must be preserved
benefits concentrated among less-skilled/less-experienced agents; treated agents with two months tenure performed comparably to untreated agents with over six months tenure
customer sentiment improved by 0.18 points, about half a standard deviation, while agent sentiment rose only 0.02 points
AI suggestions were optional and absent in a large minority of low-training-data cases
research_questions.evidence_type: field deployment with staggered rollout and observational/event-study analysis; seven-week 50-agent randomized pilot included but not separately analyzed because small
remaining_gaps: Staggered rollout supports a deployment association under the study design, but transfer to accounting requires separate task and control evaluation; customer support metrics are not financial-statement correctness.

The highest-skilled/most-experienced workers had few positive effects; authors state the setting has a stable product/question environment and results may not generalize to rapidly changing products. The paper does not estimate aggregate employment, wages, long-run skill demand or accounting accuracy.

assessment.basis: Presence and review limits of the linked named question, package workflow and original worked material. Partial does not establish accounting correctness; missing means this question packet lacks that component.

research_questions.question: When did AI assistance reduce correctness in the consultant experiment?
research_questions.scope: Two original empirical studies reviewed from public NBER/arXiv and HBS/Organization Science materials; evidence concerns workplace AI assistance, not accounting-agent performance.
research_questions.answer: A randomized field experiment with expert consultants found strong gains on tasks selected inside GPT-4 capability boundaries but materially worse correctness on one outside-frontier task, demonstrating task-level heterogeneity and overreliance risk.

source_locators.locator: Organization Science published PDF, pp. 2-5 and 8, 11-16; Table 5 p. 8, outside-frontier results p. 11 and summary/boundary conditions pp. 16-17.

observed_outcomes: 758 BCG consultants; 385 inside-frontier and 373 outside-frontier tasks; participants were randomly assigned after a baseline
For 18 inside-frontier tasks, AI groups completed 12.2% more tasks and 25.1% faster on average; the published summary reports quality improvement above 40%/more than 30% depending metric
On the outside-frontier task, controls were correct about 84.5%; GPT-only and GPT+overview groups were correct about 60.0% and 70.6%, averaging a 19 percentage-point decrease
Outside-frontier human graders were blind to condition; GPT-4 grading agreed with human grading in more than 97% of cases
The authors report benefits were largest for bottom-half-skill subjects inside the frontier, while quality could decline outside it
research_questions.evidence_type: preregistered randomized controlled laboratory-in-the-field experiment; GPT-4, control, and GPT-4 plus overview arms
remaining_gaps: Random assignment supports causal treatment effects for these GPT-4 tasks and BCG population. It does not establish performance for accounting tasks, later models, production controls, incentives, or real filing decisions; the paper itself says tasks approximate but do not fully capture on-the-job complexity.

AI assistance harmed correctness on the outside-frontier task even though participants were highly skilled and did not need to use the AI output; the authors describe overreliance and task-boundary uncertainty. Only one outside-frontier task limits breadth of the negative finding.

assessment.basis: Presence and review limits of the linked named question, package workflow and original worked material. Partial does not establish accounting correctness; missing means this question packet lacks that component.
